briefs.source_chain: MSFT/Meta guide above consensus, and buyers pull forward 2027 orders to lock scarce HBM/CoWoS capacity (sold out through 1H27) therefore supply, not appetite, is the binding constraint therefore rising HBM prices (+18% into 1Q27) signal the lock is holding and capex guides keep rising therefore the cycle extends rather than peaks therefore Buy NVDA $250 target, invalidated only by a memory-price rollover (HBM prices falling 2 consecutive months), explicitly not by a Fed rate decision
briefs.brief_chain: MSFT/Meta guide above consensus therefore GS raises 2026 capex to $751B because inference demand is outgrowing supply (appetite is the constraint) therefore rising HBM prices are a headwind that could cap capex guides therefore the cycle is closer to peaking than extending therefore Buy NVDA $250 target, invalidated by a Fed rate decision tightening financial conditions, with HBM pricing only secondary

distortions.what: Source frames the binding constraint as supply (buyers locking scarce HBM/CoWoS capacity sold out through 1H27); brief frames it as demand/appetite (inference workloads outgrowing supply) — the opposite constraint.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes: this reverses the causal story used to read future memory-pricing data, which is the variable the invalidation condition hinges on.

distortions.what: Source says rising HBM prices are evidence the cycle extends (supply lock holding); brief says rising HBM prices are a headwind that could cap capex guides — the same input produces opposite read-throughs.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes: a trader watching HBM pricing would draw the opposite conclusion about the capex cycle depending on which version they read.

distortions.what: Source's explicit stance is the cycle extends rather than peaks; brief's explicit stance is the cycle is closer to peaking than extending — a direct inversion of the thesis conviction.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes: this is a stance-direction reversal on the core call the report is making, even though the nominal NVDA rating is unchanged.

distortions.what: Source's stated invalidation is a memory-price rollover (HBM contract prices falling for two consecutive months), and it explicitly states a Fed rate decision would NOT change the picture. Brief's invalidation is a Fed rate decision tightening financial conditions, with HBM pricing demoted to secondary.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes: the brief tells a reader to watch and act on the exact condition (Fed decision) the source explicitly rules out, and downgrades the one the source actually names.
